## Description {#details}

A class template for a doubly linked list of nodes.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="T">Type of the elements linked into the list, derived from class <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links-base">double&#95;list&#95;links&#95;base</Link></code>.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="L">Type of the links node (one of <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links">double&#95;list&#95;links</Link></code> or <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/static-double-list-links">static&#95;double&#95;list&#95;links</Link></code>).</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>
A doubly linked list is a pair of head/tail pointers, allowing to iterate over the nodes.


:::info
Currently only forward iterators are provided, but there is no problem to add reverse iterators, if needed.
:::

The list elements (of type T) should be derived from the <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links-base">double&#95;list&#95;links&#95;base</Link></code> class, (usually from <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links">double&#95;list&#95;links</Link></code>) extended with the payload, that may be either the actual content or a pointer to the content.

The iterators return pointers to the list elements, i.e. to the beginning of the objects of type T.


:::info
The class does not use inheritance, but composition for the links node, to avoid inheriting unwanted methods from it.
:::

## Protected Member Attributes

### links&#95; {#a22d5f70c0589acc1c18d10e740c7a599}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T, class L = double&#95;list&#95;links&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>links&#95;type micro&#95;os&#95;plus::utils::double&#95;list&lt; T, L &gt;::links&#95;</>}
  labels = {["protected"]}>
The list top node used to point to <b>head</b> and <b>tail</b> nodes.

The node <b>next</b> pointer points to the list head, and the <b>previous</b> pointer points to the list tail.

To simplify processing, the list always has these pointers set, with an empty list node pointing to itself.

Initialize the list only at first run.

<SectionUser title="Parameters">
None.
</SectionUser>


<SectionUser title="Returns">
Nothing.
</SectionUser>

If the statically allocated list is still in the initial <em>uninitialised</em> state (with both pointers null), initialise the list to the empty state, with both pointers pointing to itself.

For non-statically initialised lists, this method is ineffective.


:::info
Must be manually called for statically allocated list before inserting elements, or any other operations.
:::
